description:
## Question

Should the devex bar for done include a per-kernel report of what the compiler did to the fast path, in the spirit of Julia's @code_warntype: bounds checks removed or kept, ifs compiled as selects, safepoints placed, copies inserted by copy-on-write ('Decide array value semantics', defk-i2e), and whether the non-finite flag kept a loop vectorisable ('Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels', defk-q1c)? If yes: its form (mix task, compile option, annotated source), what it reports, and whether it is part of the cold test.

comments.text: Resolution: no, done doesn't need it. The fast-path report is a tool for the catalog work, not part of the devex bar (which stays 'predict what is allowed', not 'what is fast') and not part of the cold test. It reports defk's own decisions exactly (bounds checks kept/dropped with the missing fact, select vs branch, safepoint placement, inlined calls, copy-on-write copies, non-finite flag sites) and clang's vectorisation through -Rpass remarks under report: :full, shown as 'unknown' when CC is not clang. Form: generated __defk_report__/0 returning data plus Defk.Report.print/1 with margin notes, so catalog tests can assert a hot loop is tight. Built when the first target workload has a gap to explain: [Add a fast-path report for kernels](defk-6cn). The verdict mentions it in Method; Limitations says whether a library would need it. Glossary: Fast-path report (CONTEXT.md).

title: Does done need a per-kernel fast-path report?
